title: Decision scenario
body: Read the situation and choose. Each choice plays out before you move on.
instruction: Work through the scenario one decision at a time.

start.body: It is late the night before an assignment is due. A coursemate messages you: they are stuck and ask if you will send them your finished work "just to look at".

_choices.consequence: They submit something very close to yours. The marker runs a similarity check, and you are both called in to explain. Your own mark is now at risk for work you did properly.

_choices.text: Say you can't share it, but offer to talk the question through
_choices.consequence: You spend fifteen minutes explaining how you approached the question. They write their own answer from there, and you have helped without putting your own work in danger.
You avoid the risk, but your coursemate is left stuck and a little hurt, and you never find out whether a quick pointer would have been enough.

collusion.body: Sharing finished work, even 'just to look at', is collusion once it shapes someone else's submission. The safest help is explaining your thinking, never handing over the artefact.

supported.body: You helped in the one way that carries no risk to either of you: you shared your reasoning, not your answer. That is exactly where the line sits.

avoided.body: You stayed safe, which matters. Next time, notice there was a middle option: you could have offered to talk the problem through without sharing anything.
